question: Is more training of the unchanged config likely beneficial or harmful given declining EV?
answer: Undetermined, not shown harmful. EV decline is ambiguous: logs favor a rising critic residual under KL-capped policy steps through a shared trunk, but no measurement separates benign target/staleness shift from critic underfitting, and development performance improved while EV fell.

measured_context.note: best checkpoint selected among 24 development evals; not held-out

recommended_next_step.description: Short unchanged-hyperparameter continuation (~48 updates) with read-only critic diagnostics.
measurements: EV vs Monte-Carlo discounted returns on completed episodes
EV split terminal vs alive-only windows
fraction of minibatches clipped by max_grad_norm
critic share of pre-clip gradient norm

decision_criteria.A_benign_shift: Var(returns) falls or post-update EV stays ~>=0.55 -> unchanged longer training justified, judged on D2 survival mean, not EV
decision_criteria.B_critic_underfit: post-update EV and MC-return EV both low/declining with flat Var(returns) -> test critic correction (separate critic, extra value epochs/PPG phase, or higher vf_coef)
decision_criteria.C_staleness: post-update EV high but pre-update EV low with large |dV| -> test lower LR or target_kl before long run

do_not: require rising EV as success gate
treat one run's trend as proof of a time effect
